reason: E1 shows a 25% microhardness increase after 600 °C annealing, attributed to elastic stresses from segregation, and notes σ-phase precipitation after 900 °C, but it does not compare slow cooling vs. rapid quenching, does not mention B2 phase, and does not establish a critical stress threshold for nucleation. The key premise linking slow cooling to segregation-driven nucleation is therefore only partially supported.
premises: Slow cooling of Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 from high-temperature BCC state causes elemental segregation
Elemental segregation builds localized elastic stresses
Elastic stresses above a critical level trigger nucleation of σ and B2 phases during annealing
Microhardness increase of ~25% after 600 °C annealing indicates elastic stress growth from segregation
Rapid quenching suppresses segregation and retains single BCC phase
